newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak, Arabs slam Israel over Jerusalem building.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak, Arabs slam Israel over Jerusalem building.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Wednesday that Israel was leading the region into a new era of violence by building a controversial Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Mubarak, whose comments echoed those of other Arab leaders, was speaking to reporters as Israeli bulldozers ripped into Jebel Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa hillside, in the disputed city for the second day despite international condemnation.

"If this settlement is built this will not be the end of the whole thing. It will be the beginning of a new era of violence which we would like to avoid," he said after he met Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke.

"The use of force and arrogance, the arrogance of power, will never lead to a solution at all. The issue of Jersualem will never be solved by the use of bulldozers. This only increases problems and hatred," Mubarak said.
Egypt was the first Arab country to make peace with Israel in 1979 and has since then brokered many rounds of Palestinian-Israeli peace talks.
But its criticism of Israeli policy has grown since the right-wing Benjamin Netanyahu became prime minister last year.

The decision by Israel to build 6,500 homes for Jews on land between Jerusalem and Bethlehem -- an area captured in the 1967 Middle East war -- was a blow to the Palestinians, who regard Arab East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state and say the construction precludes planned talks on the city's status.
Arab countries -- along with many European nations and the United States -- have criticised the construction and warned that this could lead to violence.
Syria accused Netanyahu of bringing the region to the brink of war by refusing to make peace with Damascus and building the settlements in occupied Arab lands.

"The Israeli government led by Netanyahu refuses to make peace, rejects (U.N.) resolutions 242 and 338, and opposes the land-for-peace formula. It wants to put the region on the verge of a new war...," Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said.
Moroccan King Hassan accused Israel of wanting to ignore an internationally accepted principle over Jerusalem.

"Today the Israeli government wants to make a 'tabula rasa' (clean sweep of) all that in practising a settlement policy over which each can measure the dangers," the king said in an interview on Tuesday with Italian television.

Bahrain's official news agency GNA quoted a foreign ministry official as saying: "The Israeli building of settlements aborts efforts being exerted to achieve a just and comprehensive peace in the Middle East".
The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) called for an immediate meeting of the United Nations Security Council to demand a halt to the settlement.
The request is likely to be considered on Wednesday.

The 185-member U.N. General Assembly adopted a resolution-- opposed by only Israel and the United States -- last Thursday calling on Israel to stop settlement activities. It followed a U.S. veto on March 7 of a similar Security Council resolution.

"I hope the United States does not use the veto in this issue because this will go against all the world opinion. The least it can do is to abstain because this is a right and America is a sponsor and the main country in the peace process. So I don't think it will use the veto," Mubarak said.
Tunisia's Arabic daily newspaper Assabah blamed the United States for encouraging Netanyahu's defiance of the world.

"Whatever Washington says to defend its position by using the veto... it bears an important responsibility because Netanyahu would not have had the courage to expand settlements if there was not that veto. The U.S. administration appears to protect Israel's needs and not the peace process," the paper said in an editorial.
